_meta.indication: SOHONOS is a retinoid indicated for reduction in the volume of new heterotopic ossification in adults and children aged 8 years and older for females and 10 years and older for males with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP).

pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label study with no randomization, using untreated patients from the natural history study (NHS) as a historical/external control.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric patients ≥4 years of age with a clinical diagnosis of FOP and no flare-up symptoms within the previous 4 weeks; the principal analysis population required the classic R206H mutation and no prior palovarotene exposure.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: annualized change in new heterotopic ossification (HO) volume as measured by whole-body computed tomography (WBCT); prespecified primary analysis was a Bayesian compound Poisson model with square root transformation.
pivotal_trials.n: 107 subjects treated with palovarotene (Study 301); primary analysis compared 97 palovarotene subjects to 101 NHS controls (P-FAS).
pivotal_trials.result: The prespecified Bayesian primary analysis failed: median between-study ratio of annualized new HO was 0.95 (95% CI 0.74, 1.22) with posterior probability of reduction only 0.65. Approval relied on post hoc/confirmatory analyses: using the linear mixed effects model, mean annualized new HO was 9.4 cm3/year (palovarotene) vs 20.3 cm3/year (NHS), treatment difference 10.9 cm3/year (95% CI -21.2, -0.6), nominal p=0.039.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥10%) are dry skin, lip dry, arthralgia, pruritis, pain in extremity, rash, alopecia, erythema, headache, back pain, skin exfoliation, nausea, musculoskeletal pain, myalgia, dry eye, hypersensitivity, peripheral edema, and fatigue. Serious/labeled risks include embryo-fetal toxicity and premature epiphyseal closure in growing pediatric patients.
target_moa: Palovarotene is a retinoic acid receptor gamma (RARγ)-selective agonist (retinoid); binding to RARγ antagonizes BMP/ALK2 downstream signaling by reducing SMAD 1/5/8 phosphorylation, dampening bone morphogenetic protein signaling and blocking chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation to prevent abnormal endochondral bone formation.
modality: Small molecule (orally bioavailable retinoid / RARγ-selective agonist).

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity (contraindicated in pregnancy; teratogenic) and premature epiphyseal closure in growing pediatric patients.

rems.type: The Applicant proposed a risk management plan that does not include a risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS).

advisory_committee.vote: Advisory Committee met June 28, 2023; 10 of 14 members voted that Study 301 evidence demonstrates palovarotene is effective in FOP, and 11 of 14 voted that benefits outweigh risks.

summary.text: Palovarotene received orphan drug designation for FOP (July 21, 2014) and Fast Track designation (November 25, 2014). The NDA was reviewed under Priority review as a resubmission following a Complete Response letter dated December 23, 2022, and was approved via traditional (non-accelerated) approval after an Advisory Committee meeting on June 28, 2023, as the first pharmacologic therapy for FOP.

citations.quote: On July 21, 2014, U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) designated palovarotene as an orphan drug product for the treatment of FOP.
Fast Track designation was subsequently granted on November 25, 2014, for prevention of heterotopic ossification following preosseous flare-ups in patients with FOP.
This new drug application (NDA) received a Complete Response action letter on December 23, 2022.
Palovarotene is the first pharmacologic therapy that is being approved for the treatment of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.

requirement.text: PMR 4474-3: Conduct a prospective observational registry study comparing palovarotene-exposed and unexposed FOP patients, evaluating risks of increased flare-up episodes, alterations in growth, and bone fractures, and collecting pregnancy exposure outcomes; collect 10-year safety data from a minimum of 100 subjects.

citations.quote: 4474-3 Conduct a prospective observational registry study with safety objectives of comparing palovarotene exposed and unexposed patients with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). Evaluate risks of increased flare-up episodes, alterations in growth, and bone fractures.

The registry should also collect information on women exposed to palovarotene during pregnancy to assess for adverse events related to pregnancy through the first year postpartum, and birth and developmental outcomes through the infant's first year of life.

Collect 10-year safety data from a minimum of 100 subjects, approximately half of whom will be pediatric patients (8 years to less than 18 years of age for girls and 10 years to less than 18 years of age for boys), and approximately two-thirds of whom will be exposed to palovarotene.

basis.text: FDA concluded the Applicant had demonstrated substantial evidence to reduce new HO volume but had not provided substantial evidence to support the proposed indication for prevention of HO; the indication was revised on resubmission to reduction in volume of new HO.

citations.quote: the Agency has concluded that the Applicant demonstrated substantial evidence of the effectiveness of palovarotene to reduce new HO volume in pediatric and adult patients with FOP but has not provided substantial evidence to support an indication for the prevention of HO in patients with FOP.
